Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. ## What this changes This PR joins supervised command cleanup before retiring the Linux Gateway spawn broker after failed core shutdown. **Example:** A running command prints final-marker when canceled, while Gateway core shutdown fails before process cleanup. - **Before:** Broker retirement can replace the command result with ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE. - **After:** The supervisor settles command output and process extinction before broker retirement, within the existing caller deadline. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The focused patch appears correct and has meaningful real-process boundary evidence; proof remains a controlled runtime-wrapper fixture. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The host identifies this as maintainer-authored, outside the ordinary contributor proof gate; the supplied Linux measurements exercise real broker, supervisor, relay, and anchor owners with an injected core-close error and report preserved final output and extinction. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** A command's final output and result can be lost when failed Gateway cleanup disconnects the spawn broker too early. **Reason:** Preserving command outcomes restores the existing supervision contract, and the maintainer-authored direction needs no additional product decision. ## Merge readiness ✅ **Ready for maintainer review** Keep open: this focused fix addresses a shutdown-ordering bug still present on main, with no actionable introduced defect found. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `de5f222feeadccd039c9f315bb94d0f7d98c2ae4` ## Before merge None. ## Findings None. ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: The supplied fixture injects core-close failure through the real runtime wrapper and subprocess owners rather than booting a full Gateway.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The Gateway runtime wrapper owns spawn-broker retirement; the process supervisor owns cancellation, command results, output settlement, and process-tree cleanup. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Gateway shutdown] --> B[Core close] B --> C[Runtime cleanup wrapper] C --> D[Process supervisor join] D --> E[Command output and extinction] E --> F[Admission and reader cleanup] F --> G[Spawn broker retirement] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep the existing supervisor join immediately before broker retirement, retaining the current deadline and failure semantics. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source confirms that retained core cleanup can bypass the process join and retire its broker before the CLI fallback; the author reports baseline failures, but this read-only review ran no target code. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The four-line production change is the smallest complete repair using the existing supervisor and broker owners, without replacing healthy core cleanup or the native-transport CLI fallback. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [5ad78d04962b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5ad78d04962b68ac276aa66b7be14f7ce9ccb0c7). ### Provenance checked - `Gateway broker lifetime` keeps the original intent (67cedc32e9967d01586c65dc3b18073e9beb5551: Move Linux launches to a lightweight broker while preserving cancellation, output, and relay ownership.) - `Bounded runtime cleanup` keeps the original intent (a968dc19900db67a0b4230b68d9df5e2d52c13b3: Bound process-owned shutdown waiting while retaining ordered cleanup and original fatal errors.) - `Background-process documentation` keeps the original intent (20c1a15bb56da3178a32aaa51e1207ad89172ac6: Distinguish ordinary supervised commands from durable systemd-managed processes across Gateway restarts.) - `Standalone measurement inventory` keeps the original intent (6d0157388723a4aaa80daf493f67404cc6030a76: Register maintained proof commands explicitly so unused-file analysis recognizes their documented entry points.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Pinned production change:** The introduced diff adds the existing supervisor shutdown operation before admission cleanup and broker retirement; it adds no runtime state, timer, or alternative cleanup owner. ([`src/gateway/server.ts:222`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/de5f222feeadccd039c9f315bb94d0f7d98c2ae4/src/gateway/server.ts#L222), [de5f222feead](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/de5f222feeadccd039c9f315bb94d0f7d98c2ae4)) - **Current main retains the gap:** Current main's closeBroker proceeds directly to database-admission cleanup without first joining supervised commands. ([`src/gateway/server.ts:219`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5ad78d04962b68ac276aa66b7be14f7ce9ccb0c7/src/gateway/server.ts#L219), [5ad78d04962b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5ad78d04962b68ac276aa66b7be14f7ce9ccb0c7)) - **Existing lifecycle owners:** Core close can throw for retained work before its supervisor join; the CLI's process-owner fallback runs later. Supervisor shutdown fences new launches and joins existing process extinction. ([`src/gateway/server-close.ts:648`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/de5f222feeadccd039c9f315bb94d0f7d98c2ae4/src/gateway/server-close.ts#L648), [de5f222feead](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/de5f222feeadccd039c9f315bb94d0f7d98c2ae4)) - **Regression and supplied process proof:** The regression checks final stdout, a fulfilled cancellation outcome, and native extinction after core-close failure. The PR body reports five Linux baseline/candidate pairs with lost outcomes changing from 5/5 to 0/5, using the committed runtime-wrapper fixture. ([`src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts:296`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/de5f222feeadccd039c9f315bb94d0f7d98c2ae4/src/gateway/server.spawn-broker.test.ts#L296), [de5f222feead](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/de5f222feeadccd039c9f315bb94d0f7d98c2ae4)) - **Preserved shutdown intent:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187090 established bounded process-owned waiting while ordered cleanup continues; this PR keeps that wrapper and its fatal-error preservation. ([`src/gateway/server.ts:32`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a968dc19900db67a0b4230b68d9df5e2d52c13b3/src/gateway/server.ts#L32), [a968dc19900d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a968dc19900db67a0b4230b68d9df5e2d52c13b3)) - **Feature ownership history:** Available history identifies Peter Steinberger across the original broker integration, retained startup-admission composition, reader retirement, and recent shutdown deadline repair. A deeper content search encountered unavailable historical objects; available commits and current-main blame establish routing without relying on that search. ([`src/gateway/server.ts:220`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5ad78d04962b68ac276aa66b7be14f7ce9ccb0c7/src/gateway/server.ts#L220), [5ad78d04962b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5ad78d04962b68ac276aa66b7be14f7ce9ccb0c7)) ### PR surface Source +4, Tests +61, Docs 0, Other +328.
